children: SoftBank Group (SFTBY) has secured an $11.87 billion two-year loan to help fund its massive OpenAI investment, deepening Masayoshi Son's leveraged bet on artificial intelligence just as investors are becoming more nervous about the sector. The financing gives SoftBank fresh firepower, but a nearly 13% drop in its shares Monday shows the market is increasingly focused on how much financial risk the company is taking to build its AI exposure.

SoftBank is a Japanese investment holding company with stakes across technology, telecommunications and artificial intelligence. Its portfolio strategy revolves around making large investments in high-growth technology businesses, meaning changes in asset valuations can have an outsized impact on its balance sheet and shares.
The new facility was finalized last week with commitments from about 20 banks, according to Bloomberg, exceeding SoftBank's previous $10 billion target.

It is only one piece of an increasingly complex financing strategy. SoftBank has also secured a $10 billion margin loan backed by its OpenAI stake and is considering issuing as much as $20 billion of U.S.-dollar bonds.

Meanwhile, SoftBank is due to repay $25.9 billion on September 15 from a $40 billion loan raised earlier this year to fund its OpenAI investment. That loan had originally been scheduled to mature next March.
The scale of the commitment is striking. SoftBank plans to invest nearly $65 billion in OpenAI by October and has already raised roughly $37 billion this year.

The financing comes as AI sentiment has weakened. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has called for slower AI development, while OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has said the company will not pursue an IPO this year as safety concerns are addressedInvestors Takeaway.
SoftBank's OpenAI bet is becoming as much a balance-sheet story as an AI-growth story.

Investors should watch SoftBank's net debt, interest expense, collateral pledged against investments and its ability to refinance short-term borrowings without selling valuable assets. OpenAI's revenue growth, future valuation and eventual IPO timing will also become increasingly important because SoftBank is borrowing heavily against expectations that its stake will appreciate.

A successful OpenAI listing or sustained growth could validate Son's aggressive strategy. Delays, weaker AI economics or falling private-market valuations would leave SoftBank carrying substantially more leverage against an asset with limited near-term liquidity.

title: SoftBank Raises Stakes in Its Biggest AI Bet
